name: OWEB Small Grant Program
summary: Competitive grants of up to $20,000 for on-the-ground watershed restoration in Oregon, such as riparian planting, fish passage and erosion control, reviewed by regional Small Grant Teams through the year.

eligibility.rule: Clearly demonstrate a watershed benefit to aquatic species, wildlife, or watershed health
Use and clearly identify technical guidance from at least one approved source
Be distinct from projects already funded or being considered by OWEB

documents: Cooperative landowner agreement signed by landowners

calls.label: Year-round Small Grant Area applications
calls.note: Accepted year-round until April 15, 2027; application windows set by each Small Grant Team

status.quote: Small Grant Areas accept applications year-round until April 15, 2027.

applicant_types.quote: A grant applicant may be any Tribe, watershed council, soil and water conservation district, not-for-profit corporation, school, Oregon institution of higher education, independent not-for-profit institution of higher education, or political subdivision of this state that is not a state agency.

geography.quote: awards up to $20,000 for on-the-ground restoration projects principally carried out on private lands across Oregon

access.quote: Contact your Small Grant Team Contact for application windows.

window.quote: Small Grant Areas accept applications year-round until April 15, 2027.

amount.quote: awards up to $20,000 for on-the-ground restoration projects principally carried out on private lands across Oregon

effort.quote: Small Grant Areas accept applications year-round until April 15, 2027.
At a minimum, all Teams must conduct reviews on submitted applications four times in the state fiscal year (July 1 through June 30).

eligibility.quote: OWEB may enter into agreements only with legally established entities.
Clearly demonstrates watershed benefit to aquatic species, wildlife, or watershed health.
Uses and clearly identifies (by practice code or page number and paragraph) in the small grant application technical guidance from at least one of the eight approved sources.
Distinct and different from projects already funded (or being considered for funding) by OWEB.

after_award.quote: Post-Implementation Status Reports (PISRs) are required for all OWEB restoration grants.

documents.quote: Pre-project Photos* Attach color photographs of the site showing current conditions and setting post-project monitoring photo points.
Maps * Attach a map of the project site with sufficient detail to show the location of the work to be performed.
Cooperative Landowner Agreement* Landowners must sign a cooperative agreement.

co_finance.quote: Demonstrates 25% secured match funding, based on the total OWEB award.
